meta.title: RouteOne Rates & Forms pull
meta.confidentiality: DEALER-ONLY. Lender program guides from RouteOne. Do not publish to a public repo or site.
meta.legend: "not stated" = the document is silent (NOT a no). (inf.) = desk inference, not written by the lender. ⚠ verify = conflict or uncertain read.

read_first: These sheets give **structure** (advance, term, caps, comp). **Buy rates come back on the callback**, except Westlake, Credit Acceptance and GLS, which publish rate ranges. Always run the deal on the callback before choosing a bank.
"Tier" numbers (Tier 1, Tier 4, etc.) are each lender's own and are **not** the same across banks. Most sheets don't map tiers to FICO. Where a sheet does give FICO bands, they're shown.

Advance and LTV bases differ: invoice and JD Power Clean Trade are the common bases. **Fifth Third** and **PNC** value on retail (MSRP / JD Power Clean Retail), so their 115–140% isn't comparable to the others.
takeaways: **Ally has the widest box.** It buys down to a 520 score. It has an 84-month program that includes non-prime (<620 FICO) at S–B tiers. It adds $2,000 of extra aftermarket advance through 11/2/2026. It's the only lender here with a Kia SmartLease sheet.

**Best reserve structure for strong credit:** Fifth Third (flat paid at 100%, no cap, no split; 3.00% at buy rate up to 5.00% at +1.00) and BoA (flat 1.0%–5.5% with no cap on flat). TD pays the greater of reserve or flat automatically, up to $7,500 on a 64–72 month deal. US Bank and Truist pay up to $10,000 and $8,000 per deal.

**84 months is gated almost everywhere.** It needs a young unit, low miles and strong credit: BoA 720+, Truist 680+, Wells Tiers 1–2 only, Santander "well-qualified", Ally $20K+ and ≤5-year-old, Chase ≤4-year-old.

**Deep credit, bankruptcy and repo options:** Westlake (open and dismissed BK OK, multiple repos OK, no minimum score or income), Credit Acceptance (no minimum score), GLS (FICO 400–700). Westlake Standard pays the dealer **no reserve**.

**Watch hard stops.** US Bank takes no co-signers and extends no new credit to anyone with a prior bankruptcy. TD declines a BK or repo within 36 months. PNC and Fifth Third won't write a business-titled contract. Wells requires a full tax return for self-employed income (no bank statements).

guide.why: Fifth Third flat 3.00% at buy rate (to 5.00%), paid 100%. BoA flat 1.0%–5.5%, 130% advance / 145% LTV. US Bank 740+ gets 135% front / 145% total. TD T1–T2 allow 140–150%. Ally S: up to 140% (≤63 mo), 135% at 84. PNC 800+ new up to 125% front.
guide.watch: Fifth Third and PNC advance is on a retail basis. PNC reserve cap is 2.50% and its max flat is $3,000. Buy rates aren't on the sheets, so compare callbacks.

guide.why: BoA max PTI drops to 17% under 720 FICO. US Bank gives 135% front for 675–739 (140% total at 700–739, 135% at 675–699). Truist is 640+ on both applicants.
guide.watch: US Bank: 2020–21 units over 66 mo and 2017–19 units over 48 mo need FICO >750. PNC's front-end advance is only 110% at 680–759. BoA caps 76–84 mo at 720+.

guide.call_first: **Ally (C/D tiers, ≥520 floor)**, **Santander**, **Capital One (Tiers 6–9)**, **Westlake Gold (600–699)**, **GLS (to 700)**, **Credit Acceptance Gold (600+)**
guide.why: Ally non-prime (<620) goes to 135% (S) and 115% (D/E) up to 72 mo. Santander is "full-spectrum", min income $1,750, PTI ≤22%. Capital One Tiers 6–9 are near-prime/subprime, income ≥$1,500, PTI ≤20%.
guide.watch: Truist and BoA floors are 640. Westlake Gold needs 7.5% down at 11.99%–23.99% (franchise sheet). Credit Acceptance Gold's rate is "as low as" 12.99%. Capital One may want $1,000 down on thin files.

guide.why: Westlake: open BK OK with pre-approval, dismissed OK, multiple repos OK, no minimum score or income. Credit Acceptance: no minimum score, PTI ≤25%. GLS: FICO 400–700, min income $1,800. Ally buys to 520.
guide.watch: Westlake Standard: 10% down, 140% LTV, **no dealer reserve**. Credit Acceptance Standard "as low as" 21.49%, down up to 15% or $1,000, proof of income and bank. GLS: no open BK, no repo in past 4 months, no self-employed. Chase needs BK **discharged**. TD and US Bank are out for recent or any prior BK.

guide.call_first: **Capital One Executive Diamond** (≤15 yrs, ≤200K mi), **Westlake** (no max age or mileage), **GLS** (to 180K mi), **Wells** (to 150K mi), **Santander** (≤12 yrs, 150K mi)
guide.why: Also past 125K miles: Ally (150K by segment), Capital One Base (150K), Fifth Third (140K).
guide.watch: Terms shrink fast: Wells 51 mo at 120–150K mi, Capital One 48 mo at 13+ yrs, GLS 66 mo at 120K+ mi. Under 125K: BoA, PNC, US Bank, Fifth Third (140K) and Chase (120K) are all fine. US Bank at 100K+ mi: 48 mo max (≤7 yrs old) or 36 mo (8–9 yrs).

guide.why: Ally 84-mo rates match the shorter-term rates and any approved 84-mo app can be written 76–84 mo. TD 76–84 mo front-end runs 80%–120% by tier.
guide.watch: Reserve caps shrink at 76+ mo (typically 1.50%–1.75%). Wells needs PTI ≤15%, LTV ≤120%, Tiers 1–2, no thin file, ≤3-year-old, under 45K mi. US Bank tests PTI/DTI on a 72-mo basis and caps total LTV at 120% over 72 mo.

guide.why: Ally: +$2,000 advance to 11/2 (and 30% / $10K aftermarket cap). Chase: 150% all-in plus VP add-on (greater of $4,500 or 20% of MSRP on new). Wells: total backend greater of $6,000 or 20% (max $12,500). Capital One Exec: backend to $8K plus $7K VSC. Truist: back end to $10,000.
guide.watch: Fifth Third, PNC and BoA cap total at 140% / 145% on a retail or collateral basis. Santander: VSC to $6,500, GAP to $1,200. GAP is blocked below a minimum front-end LTV at most banks (60–80%).

guide.why: US Bank says it doesn't accept co-signer applications (multiple applicants are underwritten as joint).
guide.watch: TD requires a notice to cosigner if a signer isn't on title.

guide.why: TD says personal-use vehicles bought in a company name can be booked, with an individual co-applicant. BoA Small Business: min FICO 730, ≤5-yr-old, ≤75K mi, 110% / 120%, 4+ yrs in business.
guide.watch: PNC and Fifth Third: no business loans. US Bank needs a personal applicant. Ally routes commercial-use vehicles to its Commercial Services Group.

guide.why: Santander accepts bank statements and tax returns.
guide.watch: Wells: tax return only (no bank statements). GLS: self-employed / 1099 income not accepted. Credit Acceptance: proof of income required at Standard and Silver.

guide.why: Wells lends to permanent and non-permanent residents and DACA (SSN or ITIN, with legal-status docs). Fifth Third says signers need an SSN or ITIN. TD's application list accepts SSN or ITIN.
Value bumps from each sheet. Kia is on Truist's "Standard" list ($750).
guide.watch: BoA adds a CPO adjustor automatically. Santander, Wells, PNC and Capital One: **not stated**.

flags: **Chase "Toolkit 2.0"** is the same file as the Product Reference Sheet (identical checksum). Toolkit content (EFF rules, VP guidelines, buydown, ineligible list) is **not captured**. "Marked up exactly .75bps" is probably 0.75% (75 bps). Confirm.

**BoA "Access Lending 76-mo"**: the Access Lending sheet carries the same retail grid and 76–84 rules as the standard sheet. It differs on conversion / chassis valuation (inferred as wheelchair-accessible conversions), so it isn't a separate longer-term program. Confirm with your BoA rep.
**Ally non-prime 73–75 mo (used B/C):** retail sheet 125 / 120% vs. Underwriting Policies 120 / 115%. **Ally used mileage:** UW policy 150K by segment vs. sheet 120K (light / medium duty).

**Capital One:** Which program (Executive Diamond / Diamond / Non-Diamond) Southwest Kia is on is **not stated**. Issue dates differ (Jan 2026 vs. Jul 2025). Mileage band headers are inferred from footnotes.

**Santander:** "Eligible vehicles: New, up to 12 years" is ambiguous. Flat table ends at $75,999 while max AMF is $100,000. 75/25 split side **not stated**. The dated line says "Last Updated October 2026" only.
**TD:** Tier-to-FICO map **not stated**. Tier 9 column blank on advance grids. PDF dates differ from RouteOne (6/30 vs. 7/1/26).
**Truist:** PDF text layer is garbled; I used page images. FICO bureaus vary by state (Equifax in TX). Max reserve $8,000 vs. flat table to $2,600.
**Wells Fargo:** Guide is effective **today (10/15/26)**. No FICO, tier, BK or rate info, only 84-mo gate. 10-yr-old row gap. Comp formula **not stated**.
**Credit Acceptance:** RouteOne eff 1/12/26 vs. PDF footer 5/27/26. Advance and comp **not stated**.
**Westlake:** Prime/Presidential warranty footnote cut off. Max term **not stated**. Only two of the Westlake programs were downloaded (Predictable Prime, RV, Powersports, 2026 Guidelines were not).
**Fifth Third / PNC:** Advances are on a retail-value basis, so compare with care.

**Missing:** Kia Finance America retail terms (only a 2013 lease tax packet). No sheets for AmeriCredit, American Credit Acceptance, Consumer Portfolio Services, Driveway Finance, Exeter, Flagship, RouteOne Marketing.
**Not captured anywhere:** Buy-rate sheets (come on callbacks) for most banks. Most income and PTI minimums for Ally, Chase, TD, PNC, Fifth Third.
corrections: **TD flat fees:** notes had the 48–63 mo ladder wrong. Correct ladder is above (buy 1% to +200 bps 5% by term bracket, with $ caps).
**Westlake tiers** are Standard / Gold / Platinum / Titanium by score band (0–599 / 600–699 / 700–749 / 750+), not A–D.
**Truist** advance, PTI/DTI and term grids are by tier (full grid above). Notes were a simplification.
**BoA** pays a flat table to 5.5%, not only 1%; it also has reserve caps 2.50 / 2.00 / 1.75%.
**Santander** gives one LTV (145%), not separate front / total.
**Ally SmartLease** S-tier rates in the notes were for the Carnival only; rates vary by model.
**Capital One** details (not in notes) are now extracted.

sections.title: Credit/rates
sections.text: Prime = FICO ≥620 (S–C tiers). Non-prime = <620 (S–E). Min bureau score 520 retail, 550 lease. Rates come on the callback. Caps are 24.00% new / 25.00% used or state cap.

sections.title: Term
sections.text: New/CSU–MY2021 up to 84. 2020–2016 up to 75 (needs FICO ≥620, AMF >$5,000, <100K mi). 2015–14 up to 63 (S–B only). **84-month program:** all S/A/B retail, new and used. Same rate for 76–84. Min AMF $20,000. Model years ≤5 yrs old, ≤75,000 mi. Max DFI 1.50%. Advance: new S 135 / A 125 / B 115; used 130 / 120 / 115; non-prime S 125 / A 120 / B 115.

sections.title: Vehicle
sections.text: Min AMF $5,000. Used mileage up to 150K by segment (UW policy). Salvage, flood and frame-damage titles are out. Collateral: new = invoice plus allowed DIOs. Used = JD Power Clean Trade (KBB lending value in AZ, CA, CO, HI, ID, NM, NV, OR, UT, WA, WY) or auction price (120 days SmartAuction / 90 days other). **CPO adds $1,000.**

sections.title: Back end
sections.text: Total aftermarket greater of $5,000 or 30% of EDC/AWV, max $10,000 (<$80K) / $15,000 (≥$80K). VSC greater of $5,000 or 15%. Maintenance greater of $2,000 or 10%. Tire & wheel greater of $1,500 or 7%. GAP by state per matrix. **+$2,000 additional advance** for aftermarket sales through 11/2/26 (S–C tiers, prime and non-prime, 84 mo included; stackable with Dealer Rewards; not with SmartLease/ComTRAC).

sections.title: Dealer comp
sections.text: Max DFI 2.50% (≤60 mo) / 2.00% (61–75) / 1.50% (76–84); D/E tiers 2.00%. **Min DFI $150 / $250 / $350 / $450 / $500** by AMF band (>$5K / $25K / $35K / $45K / $75K). A dealer acquisition fee can be assessed at callback (can't be passed to the customer).

sections.title: Stips/income/PTI
sections.text: PTI/DTI/income minimum **not stated**. Approvals valid 30 days. Contract package due within 15 days. Credit card down limit $5,000.

sections.title: Notable
sections.text: SmartLease Kia (rates vary by model; S-tier ex. Carnival 11.09% / 9.49% / 9.54% / 9.29% for 12–27 / 36–42 / 48 / 60 mo; acquisition fee $695; tier markups A +1.00, B +2.50, C +5.65, D +8.95; Ally Lease Cash $0 on listed models). Ally 300 pays $300 on a lease-to-retail buyout (used, standard rate; not chargeback-able).
